api: Local REST API that is largely OpenAI-compatible, so most existing code can be repointed with a base-URL change.
cons: Model licences still apply and still need review
Easy for staff to install without oversight
name: Ollama
pros: Trivial to install compared with raw self-hosting
files: Depends on the model served. Text and, for multimodal models, images.
value: Turns self-hosting from an infrastructure project into a single install. Pulls and runs open-weight models locally with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which means existing code usually points at it unchanged.
engine: Not a model. A runtime and model manager that serves open-weight models locally.
latency: Bounded entirely by local hardware. Small models are fast on a modern laptop; large ones need serious GPU capacity.

pricing.includes: Full local runtime and model library

quality: Exactly the quality of whichever open-weight model is loaded. Ollama adds no capability and takes none away.
tagline: The simplest way to run open-weight models entirely on your own machine.
use_cases: Running an assistant on confidential material with no network path at all
Local development against a model without per-token cost
Air-gapped or high-sensitivity environments where no external API is permitted
governance_note: This is the strongest available answer to 'we cannot send this data anywhere'. It converts an AI vendor risk assessment into an endpoint security question, which most organizations already know how to run. The residual risks move to the model licence and to unmanaged installs on staff laptops, so pair adoption with a licence review and an endpoint policy.
training_optout: Not applicable. Nothing leaves the machine, which is the entire reason to use it.
